entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary:
The International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD) stands as the cornerstone of global health information, a systematic diagnostic tool for epidemiology, health management, and clinical applications that has profoundly shaped the understanding and control of human disease for over a century. Developed and maintained by the World Health Organization (WHO), this comprehensive classification system provides a standardized language for reporting mortality and morbidity across nations, enabling comparative analysis of health trends, resource allocation, and the efficacy of public health interventions from the late 19th century through the digital age.

The genesis of the ICD can be traced to the need for uniform mortality statistics, initiated in 1853 by the First International Statistical Congress in Brussels, which tasked Florence Nightingale and William Farr with developing a common classification of causes of death. Farr's work, leading to the "International List of Causes of Death," was formally adopted in 1893. Subsequent revisions occurred roughly every decade, often under the stewardship of the International Statistical Institute, until the World Health Organization assumed responsibility for the Sixth Revision (ICD-6) in 1948, expanding its scope to include morbidity. This pivotal shift transformed the ICD from a mortality-focused list into a comprehensive diagnostic and health management tool, incorporating mental health disorders and injuries alongside infectious and chronic diseases, reflecting the evolving understanding of health.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems established the universal language for understanding and combating disease, fundamentally transforming public health, clinical practice, and medical research globally since the late 19th century. Its continuous evolution and adoption by nearly all nations have enabled unprecedented comparative analysis of health data, saving countless lives by informing disease prevention and treatment strategies.
